data.hypothesis: Replacing Gm1’s static collapsed (z,y) worksharing with Gm2’s contiguous z-slab ownership may improve locality or reduce scheduling overhead while retaining Gm1’s row-based stencil and guarded SIMD loop. The measured aggregate means are close (Gm1 0.054595 s; Gm2 0.055090 s), so any benefit from this combination remains unverified.
data.notes: Retains the recurrence, initialization, bounds, and buffer parity. Threads own disjoint z slabs across all six steps; the barrier before each dependent step ensures writes are complete. The controller must establish correctness and performance.
transformations: Retained Gm1’s row-base stencil expression and compile-time-guarded OpenMP SIMD loop over contiguous x.
Adapted Gm2’s persistent team and deterministic contiguous z-slab partitioning, capped by the requested thread budget and the interior z extent.
Added synchronization between dependent timesteps while retaining timestep parity, full buffer initialization, and the specified update bounds.
